correctness.rationale: Separate exact arithmetic in the quadratic field reconstructed the 15 lines from the six poles and classified all 105 line pairs into 15 double, 10 triple and 6 quintuple points. Replacing only the higher-multiplicity points by exceptional stars gives a connected graph with 31 vertices, 75 edges, and genera zero on the components; its arithmetic genus is 45. Distinct tangent directions separate on blowup, and the vertex degrees 6, 3 and 5 establish stability. Two independently built reduced cofactors give determinant 595146407909049887=11^4·17^5·31^5. Modular nullities 4, 5 and 5 match the respective determinant valuations; this forces all positive Smith valuations to be one and gives C527 plus four C5797 factors. Nonzero determinant and the exact factorization exclude other primes. The graph-to-Néron conclusion applies only to the specified proper regular split semistable model with reduced special fiber and thickness one, by the component-group comparison theorem.
residual_risks: The independent replay proves the finite incidence and group claims directly through cofactors and ranks; it does not rely on or independently derive the auxiliary full characteristic polynomial. The Néron application does not assert existence of a particular smoothing or permit arbitrary edge thicknesses.

value.rationale: The partial resolution is dictated by the geometry: blow up the non-nodal points and preserve the ordinary nodes. This gives a natural stable curve and a concrete component group for eligible degenerations. The exact statement that all primary torsion is elementary, with the indicated ranks at three primes, is information beyond the known line census and a spanning-tree count.
residual_risks: The consequence is for the specified stable boundary and regular unit-thickness models, not for the Picard group of the surface or a different contraction or blowup.
